assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based framework and the empirical work on the China trade shock changed how economists and policymakers think about technology, trade, labour demand and wage polarization. The work is broad in influence, empirically credible and tied to central questions of distribution and adjustment. It also connects naturally to growth and structural change.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure for the task approach and for the local-labour-market adjustment evidence. Hanson and Autor (with Dorn) jointly carry the China-shock work. Katz anchors the earlier skill-premium and education-technology race literature. Dorn is a close co-author on the trade-shock papers, and Frank Levy and Richard Murnane, who co-developed the task approach, are not on the list. A three-person set is defensible but leaves out real contributors.
assessment.maturity: The key papers date from roughly 1992 to 2016. They have a long record of replication, refinement and debate, including on the size and persistence of the China shock. The contribution is mature and widely validated.
uncertainties: Which of Katz, Hanson and Dorn is the best third or second laureate
Attribution gaps for contributors outside the credited names
Ongoing debate over the persistence of the China shock and the magnitude of task-displacement effects

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, the New Keynesian Phillips curve and the interest-rate-rule framework form the workhorse of modern monetary policy analysis and central bank practice. The influence on both theory and practice is exceptionally large.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty. At least eight credited individuals contributed across staggered contracts and pricing (Taylor, Calvo), the micro-founded framework (Woodford, Gali, Gertler), and medium-scale DSGE estimation (Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets). Calvo pricing and the Taylor rule and contracts are the most identifiable foundational pieces. Woodford is the systematic synthesizer, but the choice of three necessarily omits Gali, Gertler, Christiano and Eichenbaum.
assessment.maturity: The foundational work dates from the 1980s and 1990s, and the framework has been tested through several crises. It is highly mature, and the delay reflects the attribution problem rather than any lack of confirmation.
uncertainties: Many strong contributors and no clean three-person cut
Lingering debate over how well the New Keynesian framework performed in and after the financial crisis and the 2021-22 inflation
Whether Calvo's contribution is viewed as foundational enough relative to Gali or Gertler

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run top-income and wealth series, built from tax data, reopened the empirical study of distribution and strongly influenced public debate and policy. The scientific contribution is data construction and measurement as well as concepts. The societal relevance is very high.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the clear originators of the top-income series. Zucman extends the work to wealth and offshore holdings. Atkinson, who is deceased, was an important precursor and co-developer. The trio is a natural grouping, although the contribution of each differs in kind.
assessment.maturity: The top-income work dates from the early 2000s and is well established. The wealth-distribution and offshore estimates are newer and contested, and methodological critiques, for example on capitalization methods and survey reconciliation, remain active.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes over wealth-share estimates
Whether the committee values data construction as highly as identified causal or theoretical contributions
Interpretive and theoretical claims in the Piketty framework, such as r>g, are less settled than the measurement

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learning methods for causal inference (double/debiased ML, causal forests, heterogeneous effect estimation) bring high-dimensional methods into credible empirical work across many fields. Methodological reach is broad and practical use is growing quickly.
assessment.attribution: Chernozhukov (with co-authors) developed the debiased ML and high-dimensional inference theory. Athey and Wager developed causal forests and related heterogeneous-effect tools. Imbens, a co-author of Athey and a 2021 laureate, complicates the picture. Many co-authors, including Belloni, Hansen and Newey, did core work in the double/debiased ML literature.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from about 2016 to 2018, so the confirmation horizon is shorter. Adoption is substantial, but the long-run importance of the methods and the settling of best practice are still developing.
uncertainties: Relatively recent timing
Credit shared with co-authors outside the credited set
Overlap with the 2021 prize on causal inference methodology

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HANK models integrate household heterogeneity and liquidity constraints into monetary and fiscal policy analysis. They changed the transmission-mechanism view, showing the importance of indirect effects and marginal propensities to consume. The work is influential in macro and is also computationally and conceptually innovative.
assessment.attribution: The trio is a natural and tight group, with Kaplan-Moll-Violante (2018 AER) as the core paper. Important precursors and parallel contributors exist in the heterogeneous-agent literature (Aiyagari, Bewley, Huggett, Krusell-Smith, and others), so the field's foundations are broader than this trio. I have a methodological affinity with this literature, since I have worked on heterogeneous-agent computational methods, and I disclose it.
assessment.maturity: The central contribution dates from about 2014 to 2018. It is influential but still young, and the full empirical performance of HANK in policy practice remains in progress.
uncertainties: Relatively recent for Nobel recognition
Whether the committee views the contribution as a synthesis of older heterogeneous-agent work
Empirical disciplining of the models is still evolving

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data opened up measurement of intergenerational mobility and of neighbourhood effects on opportunity. The work is high-impact, creative in measurement and policy relevant. It extends a long literature (Solon, Mulligan and others) with much richer data.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader. Hendren and Friedman are major collaborators, but the grouping is partly a team around one researcher. The credit relative to earlier mobility scholars is a real question, and Chetty's wider work (taxation, teachers, mobility) may be the more natural basis for any recognition.
assessment.maturity: The main mobility results date from 2014 to 2022. Replication and extension are ongoing, but the work is still young for Nobel-level confirmation. Debates about causal interpretation of place effects continue.
uncertainties: Timing and whether the contribution is consolidated enough
Attribution concentrated in one individual, with weaker case for co-laureates
Interpretation of neighbourhood causal effects

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law and finance opened a large empirical literature on how legal institutions shape financial development and corporate governance, an important link between institutions and growth. The influence is wide across finance, law and political economy.
assessment.attribution: The core is the LLSV (La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer, Vishny) papers of the late 1990s. Vishny is credited but a cap of three forces a cut, and the choice among the four is hard. Shleifer's broader contribution across behavioural finance and corporate governance strengthens his case. The legal-origins thesis has been criticized.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers are around 25 to 30 years old. Their influence is clear but the empirical claims, especially on legal origin as a causal factor, have been heavily questioned over time.
uncertainties: Robustness and causal interpretation of legal-origins results
Which three of the four should be credited
Controversies surrounding some of the laureate candidates could weigh in deliberations

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-firm trade models explain exporter selection and reallocation gains from trade. They moved the field's micro foundations and connect to firm dynamics and productivity growth. Influence on theory and empirical trade is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the core contribution. Helpman has deep earlier contributions (monopolistic competition in trade, with Krugman, who is already a laureate) and heterogeneous-firm extensions with Melitz and Yeaple. Redding is an important later contributor on quantitative models. Bernard, Eaton and Kortum, among others, contributed parallel ideas and are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from about 2003 and has been thoroughly tested, with the foundations well confirmed. Helpman also appears in another candidate (B017), so any recognition would need coordination across candidates.
uncertainties: Parallel contributions from Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum
Overlap of Helpman across two ballots
Trade has had fewer recent prizes, but the committee's field balance is uncertain
